summary: This article explains how the Arabian oryx survives in the desert, why it vanished from the wild, and how zoos, reserves, and rangers brought it back.
introduce: Read the title “The Arabian Oryx Comes Back” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: no longer living anywhere, or no longer living in a certain place
being kept and cared for by people, such as in a zoo, instead of living free
to have babies or to help animals have babies

challengeTerms.def: the work of protecting nature, wild animals, and plants
to bring an animal or plant back to a place where it used to live
the number of animals or people living in a place

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people can fix the harm they have done to wild animals? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the Arabian oryx went from extinct in the wild to living free again.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review extinct, captivity, and breed, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use conservation, reintroduce, and population in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
